evidence.field: 字形、說文、形義通解、用例
evidence.text: The entry shows one small-seal example and four Chu manuscript examples for 快, but no oracle-bone or bronze forms. It gives the Shuowen analysis 喜也。从心，夬聲, and presents ‘joyful/pleased’ as the original sense. It cites 易·旅 心未快也 for ‘pleased/satisfied’, Song Yu’s 風賦 快哉此風 for pleasure, 荀子·大略 for an uninhibited sense, 史記·項羽本紀 快戰 for vigorous action, a Tang Du Fu line for ‘sharp’, and a modern literary example for adverbial ‘soon’. These are textual citations, not independently dated manuscript witnesses or a complete semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 快

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry treats 𢘦 as a variant of 快 and says it derives directly from the seal form through clerical transformation; it reports that the Zhengzitong says 𢘦 was the original form and 快 a popular abbreviation, with later omission of 叏 in favor of 夬. This is an explicit historical analysis from the dictionary, but the precise chronology and documentary basis are not established by this page alone.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》: 𢘦 (快)

evidence.field: official copyright notice for queried glyph images and attributes
evidence.text: The rights notice explicitly places character-form images and glyph-attribute information obtained through its query interface under CC0 1.0 to the extent allowed by law. It does not grant rights to unrelated linked dictionary text or other Academia Sinica sites.

evidence.text: The database overview describes a character-form evolution resource maintained by Academia Sinica’s Center for Digital Cultures and reports its collection of character heads and forms. Search did not locate a query result page or direct Xiaoxuetang glyph image for 快 in this invocation.

evidence.source: CUHK guide to the Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: database purpose and form access conventions
evidence.text: The guide describes the database as a resource for Chinese language teaching and explains its ancient-character categories. It is a database guide, not a reuse license for its character-page text or images.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫使用指南

evidence.source: Local Baxter–Sagart transcription cross-check; external source inspected for component analysis
evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv rows 1121 and 1913; CUHK page lines 159–172
evidence.text: Local rows give 夬 U+592C: Modern guài, Middle Chinese kwaejH, Old Chinese *[k]ʷˤret-s; and 快 U+5FEB: Modern kuài, Middle Chinese khwaejH, Old Chinese *[k]ʷʰˤret-s. The systems remain distinct from Zhengzhang (2003), which the dossier reports as 快 *kʰʷraːds and 夬 *kʷraːds. CUHK independently describes 夬 as 快’s phonetic element and gives the shared Guangyun rhyme category and 快’s 苦夬切. Modern readings alone do not prove an ancient sound relation. The cited page does not provide the matching pair of reconstructed values.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 快

evidence.source: Unicode Unihan official character endpoint; local Unihan cross-check
evidence.field: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt rows 57914 and 73821; GetUnihanData endpoints attempted
evidence.text: Local Unihan data records current kMandarin 夬 guài and 快 kuài. The official per-character Unicode Unihan endpoints for U+592C and U+5FEB were attempted but inaccessible in this session, so these local readings have no verified per-character Unicode click-through evidence here. They are modern metadata and not evidence of an ancient phonetic relation.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup

search_audit.query: 快 说文 早期字形 楚简 快 字形 漢語多功能字庫
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the CUHK 快 entry and Taiwan MOE variant entry. Ctext returned 403 when opened. The CUHK page supports the 心/夬 phonosemantic analysis, listed historical forms, Shuowen gloss, and literary citations; the MOE page records an account of 𢘦 and 快. No precise dated earliest attestation was established.

search_audit.query: 快 小篆 楚簡 隸書 字形 漢典 字源
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the CUHK entry, which lists a small-seal form and four Chu manuscript examples. It provides no stroke-by-stroke account of graphic change.

search_audit.query: 快 Xiaoxuetang 字形演變 快
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the database overview; direct guessed character-form pages were inaccessible. No exact 快 glyph result or direct image was verified, so no Xiaoxuetang image is proposed.

search_audit.outcome: Search results did not establish a Commons historical glyph asset for 快. No reusable Commons image candidate with verified identity and rights was found.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the official CC0 notice, which applies to queried glyph images and glyph attributes. The example character page was for 流, not 快, and is not used as a candidate.

search_audit.query: site:xiaoxue.iis.sinica.edu.tw 快 小學堂 字形
search_audit.outcome: Search/open did not verify these direct candidate pages; both were inaccessible. No glyph image URL is proposed.

gaps: No securely dated first attestation of 快 was established. The CUHK page lists Chu manuscript forms and literary citations, but does not independently date the manuscript witnesses or establish a complete chronological order among senses.

The semantic link from ‘joyful/pleased’ to ‘rapid’ is described by the Shuowen commentary as extension in the dossier; the finer steps and dates are unestablished. Other listed meanings, including sharp, indulgent, and soon, are cited but not fully ordered.

The earliest depicted referent and original pronunciation of 夬 are uncertain. The available evidence supports 夬 as a sound component within 快, not a whole-graph loan based on the name of a depicted object. The object's name is not independently recovered here.
MOE’s account says 𢘦 is an original form and 快 a later abbreviated form, but exact chronology and underlying witnesses need corroboration. No graphic corruption claim is established.

Exact official Unicode GetUnihanData records for 快 and 夬 could not be opened, and no accessible exact rows were verified in this stage; modern readings above are reported from local cross-check metadata only.

No image candidate is returned: searches did not establish an accessible direct glyph image with exact identity and provenance. Xiaoxuetang's CC0 terms were verified, but no 快 query result was located. CUHK page glyphs were not visually inspected and its page does not itself provide reuse permission for image assets.

limitations.text: No historical glyph image is proposed because this research did not verify an accessible direct image URL, exact image identity, and reuse provenance for 快. The CUHK page documents historical form categories, but its image display was not inspected and its image reuse rights were not established. Xiaoxuetang permits reuse of glyph images obtained through its query interface under CC0 1.0, but no exact 快 glyph result or direct image URL was retrieved.
